raw_response:
*Settling in to think this through as an old farmer would...*

---

Well, two mu isn't much land. It's what the family's been working since the land was divided. My two sons are in Handan, one does construction, the other runs a small shop — so the land isn't really what feeds us anymore. But I've been growing wheat and maize on these two mu for forty years, and as long as my legs still carry me out to the field, I'm going to keep farming it. The grain feeds the house, and whatever's left we sell or give to relatives.

I don't do anything fancy. I do what my father did and what the neighbors do. Old Liu down the lane, he farms about the same as me, and we pretty much plant and fertilize the same days. The village is on the same schedule — the wheat combine comes through in early June, then everybody races to get maize in the ground before the rain window closes.

**For the wheat.** I'll plant around mid-October, same as always, after the land has a bit of moisture. I buy seed from the supply shop in the town — about 30 jin per mu, whatever they're selling that year. Before I plow, I spread two bags of compound fertilizer (the 15-15-15 kind) across the two mu — so one bag per mu at the base. Then in spring, when the wheat is greening up and starting to stand tall, I put down one bag of urea for the two mu together. That's how it's done here. If the wheat looks pale, I'll scatter a bit more. My land gives me about 800 jin per mu in a normal year, sometimes less if the spring is dry.

Irrigation — I pump from the village well. I give it one watering before winter so the roots settle in, one when it greens up in March, and one more when it's heading out in April. Three times, same as the neighbors. The electric meter adds up, but you can't skip the heading-time water or the grain won't fill.

Weeds I spray once in spring with whatever the shop recommends. Bugs I usually don't bother with unless I see aphids bad.

**For the maize.** Right after the wheat combine leaves, within three or four days, I get the maize in. No time to plow — the neighbor boy comes with the no-till planter and drills it straight into the stubble, charges me 40 yuan per mu. Hybrid seed, the shop gives me whatever variety everyone's buying. When the maize is about knee-high, I side-dress with urea — one bag across the two mu. Sometimes if it rains well I don't need to water. If July is dry I'll give it one watering at tasseling. That's the important one.

Maize gives me about 900 jin per mu if the weather's kind. Harvest is end of September, my wife and I pick it by hand because the plots are small and I don't want to pay for the combine on just two mu.

**On cost.** I figure across the year for both crops together on the two mu, I spend maybe 1200-1400 yuan on inputs — seed, fertilizer, electricity for the pump, the planter fee, sprays. Not much, but I watch every bag. Fertilizer went up again this year, so I'm not putting on any extra.
